persona.who: 22, wants to be a filmmaker, father is a government doctor who wants him to do MBBS or at least MBA. Fights every dinner.
persona.note: papa says films are for rich kids and I should do MBA. we fight every night. I love him and I also feel like he doesn't see me at all. mummy cries in the kitchen

understanding.bridge: What your father calls a rich kid's hobby, the Gita calls a calling: and a calling that is yours cannot be made smaller by the one who does not see it.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being dismissed to standing in your own truth with the words to say so, without breaking the bond.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being unseen by your father, and the grief of it, named without blame.
week_beats.story: A young man who questioned an elder's dismissal and stood in his truth shows you what being seen looks like from the inside.

understanding.core_struggle: A student under twenty-five whose father dismisses his love of film, insists on an MBA, and with whom he fights every night while his mother cries.
understanding.mirror: Every night the same fight, and in the kitchen your mother cries.
understanding.insight: You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: I keep fighting with my parents. Being seen as less than you are by the people who ought to know you best, and the anger of watching the life you built get called a phase.
queries.diagnose: When a parent sees only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture starts to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly; hold your ground on what is yours; do your own duty without shrinking to fit their picture.
queries.story: A young man whose father dismissed his calling, who stood in his truth and found a way to be seen without breaking the bond.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

matched.label: My parents' expectations weigh on me

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Arjuna is on the battlefield, listening to Krishna talk about the nature of duty. Krishna tells him that it is better to follow your own path, even if you stumble, than to copy someone else's perfectly. The idea is simple. Do the work that comes from your own nature, offer it without worrying about the results, and you will not be wrong. It is a quiet permission to stop trying to be what the world wants you to be.
verse.for_you: You are living inside a path that was not drawn by your own hand. The grief of being unseen by your father is real, and it is not your fault. Your calling is not a rich kid's hobby.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Twelve-year-old Ashtavakra is stopped at King Janaka's gate because he is 'only a boy'.
verse.sanskrit: न ज्ञायते कायवृद्ध्या विवृद्धि- / र्यथाऽष्ठीला शाल्मलेः संप्रवृद्धाः / ह्रस्वोऽल्पकायः फलितो विवृद्धो / यश्चाफलस्तस्य न वृद्धभावः
verse.line: Growth isn't size. A small tree bearing fruit has grown more than a tall, empty one.
verse.translation: Growth isn't measured by the size of the body. A short tree that bears fruit has grown; a tall one that bears none has not.
verse.why: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.

prasang.title: Ashtavakra at Janaka's court
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra, born bent in eight places by his father's curse, learns at twelve that his father drowned after losing a debate to the court sage Bandi. Turned away at the gate as a child, he argues his way in and defeats Bandi.
prasang.story_hook: The gatekeeper laughed at the twelve-year-old who wanted to debate the king's greatest scholar.
prasang.lesson: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.

verse.meaning: At King Janaka's gate, the guards stop a twelve-year-old boy named Ashtavakra. They see his small, curved body and decide he is too young to enter. They measure him by his size and dismiss him. But Ashtavakra knows that growth is not measured by the body. A short tree that bears fruit has grown more than a tall one that stands empty. The verse says we should not dismiss anyone for being young. It asks us to look for what a person carries, not how they look.
verse.for_you: Your father sees the shape of your life and calls it a hobby. He does not see the work you do. Let him see the fruit of your days, not the size of your room. Your calling is the fruit, not the frame.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From 'The Way of the Free Ascetic'.
verse.sanskrit: ब्रह्माण्डं मण्डलीमात्रं किं लोभाय मनस्विनः । शफरीस्फुरितेनाब्धिः क्षुब्धो न खलु जायते ॥
verse.line: The ocean is not stirred by a small fish's flick. Petty things needn't shake you.
verse.translation: For the high-minded the whole universe is a mere ring; what is there in it to be greedy for? The ocean is not churned up by the flicker of a little fish.
verse.why: Let others' labels and small things pass; contentment makes you rich.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: The way of the free ascetic
prasang.summary: Portraits of the wandering sage: unbothered when people argue over his caste, sleeping under the sky like a king, and finally bidding farewell to the five elements.
prasang.lesson: Let others' labels and small things pass; contentment makes you rich.

verse.for_you: Your father calls your love of film a rich kid's hobby. His words are small fish flicking in a big ocean. Let them pass. Your calling is yours, and no flicker can stir your true depth.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Hanuman has just approached Ram and Lakshman, and Ram notices how the stranger speaks. The words are not too long or vague or rushed. They are not strained. They come out in an even, middle tone. The point is that calm words build trust faster than fear. When fear jumps ahead of facts, it only makes things worse. A steady voice shows you are grounded, and that steadiness invites the other person to listen.
verse.for_you: When you speak to your father tonight, try to keep your voice even. Do not rush or argue. Just state one clear thing you want. An even tone will do more to make him hear you than a raised voice ever could.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha that a person who is free inside does not sink in the world. They do the work that is right in front of them. They see friend and foe with the same eye. They let go of wanting and not wanting. They say what is agreeable to all and speak gently. They read the hearts of others. Because of this, they neither grieve nor crave. They live fully in the world while staying calm and unhurried inside.
verse.for_you: When your father raises his voice at night, do not let his words pull you under. Speak to them with an even voice, and read what they truly need. You do not have to fight back to stay standing. You can meet the noise with a calm mind and keep your own ground.

story.title: Nachiketa questions his father's gift
story.story_hook: Nachiketa watched his father give away cows too old to give milk, and could not keep quiet.
story.summary: A father makes a show of giving away all he owns, but the cows are old and dry. His young son Nachiketa keeps asking who he will be given to, until the father snaps, 'To Death!' The boy goes, and tells his father to keep his word.
story.lesson: A child's honest question can show up an adult's empty gesture.

script: Arjuna stands on the battlefield. He has laid down his bow. He tells Krishna he cannot fight. He sees only ruin in the faces of his family. And Krishna replies:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

Krishna says it is better to follow your own path, even if you stumble, than to copy someone else's perfectly. This is about doing the work that fits your own nature. It is an honest offering. It is not about the results. It is about the work itself. This is easier said than done. When someone in your own house does not see you, it feels like you are the one who is wrong. But the right path is the one that is yours.

Think about the films you love. That is your own path. It is not a rich kid's hobby. It is your truth. When your father talks about an MBA, he is talking about a path that is not yours. You do not have to walk that path to be his child.
What is the one small thing you did today that felt truly yours?

depth.life: You are fighting every night because your father insists on an MBA for you. Your mother cries in the kitchen. You feel torn and unseen in your own home.
depth.points: Your own nature has a calling. It is not a rich kid's hobby. Doing work that fits you, even if it is imperfect, is the right path.
depth.practice: Write down one thing you love about film, just for yourself, and read it once.
depth.question: What would it feel like to walk your own path, even if it is imperfect?
